title: Quantum estimation, channel orders, and private capacity
abstract: Recent examples have shown that zero private capacity need not imply antidegradability and that two channels with zero private capacity can nevertheless transmit private information together. Existing entropic channel orders compare what a receiver and its environment can learn and thereby bound capacities. We connect these orders to the recent constructions through binary estimation, whose minimum mean-square error is governed by measured $χ^2$ divergence. A new integral representation shows how measured $χ^2$ on a qubit extension recovers quantum $χ^2$. It lets us pass from complete measured-$χ^2$ ordering to complete quantum-$χ^2$, relative-entropy, and less-noisy ordering. Zhu and Wang used a signed lift to show that their qutrit channel has zero private capacity. We show that Hermitian-smoothed measured-$χ^2$ ordering characterizes when such lifts exist, even with a quantum reference. Environmental dominance in binary estimation at every blocklength yields a finite-code reliability--secrecy bound. These results explain why complete comparison prevents activation with antidegradable helpers whereas regularized comparison alone does not. Building on that qutrit example, we establish this stability for a range of noisy Werner--Holevo channels, determine sharp private-capacity and antidegradability thresholds, and compute exact complementary capacities in a nondegradable range. By contrast, we extend Pauli half-erasure activation to all $1/2\le p<1$ and establish the same range for a new four-level family. Reference-assisted measured-$χ^2$ witnesses show why these activating constructions lack complete comparison.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive framework to analyze the private capacity of quantum channels by connecting it to the measured $\chi^2$ divergence derived from binary estimation. It establishes a rigorous hierarchy of channel orderings and provides sharp, quantitative bounds for capacity and antidegradability, explaining when and why these information measures are equivalent or distinct.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the private capacity of quantum channels and establish structural conditions for when zero private capacity occurs, especially when this condition does not imply antidegradability.
main_result: The authors establish a hierarchy connecting complete measured-$\chi^2$ ordering to quantum $\chi^2$ ordering, providing sharp thresholds for private capacity and antidegradability for various noisy channels.
method: The work heavily utilizes measured $\chi^2$ divergence derived from binary estimation tasks, connecting these measurements to fundamental quantum information measures like private capacity and relative entropy.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on general quantum channels ($\Lambda$) acting on qubits and qutrits, involving an input, a receiver, and an environment. Specific models include Werner-Holevo channels and Pauli half-erasure channels.
key_observables: Private Capacity $P(N)$, Minimum Mean-Square Error (MMSE), measured $\chi^2$ divergence ($\chi^2_m$), and various channel orderings ($\preceq$).
important_parameters: Blocklength ($n$), the degree of the channel (e.g., qutrit extension), and the error parameters ($p$ in erasure channels).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on connecting operational tasks (like binary estimation) to theoretical channel properties, and in some parts, assumes specific structural forms for the channels (e.g., for the simulator construction).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the use of measured $\chi^2$ divergence in binary estimation at both the receiver and the environment.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first connecting private capacity to channel orders using measured $\chi^2$ (Chunk 1). It then develops the mathematical framework by relating $\chi^2_m$ to MMSE and establishing the hierarchy of orderings (Chunk 2). Finally, it applies these tools to analyze specific channel properties like antidegradability and capacity bounds using qutrit and general channel constructions (Chunks 3 & 4).
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into quantum channel capacity, linking concrete estimation tasks (like MMSE) to abstract concepts like antidegradability, which is crucial for understanding information leakage in quantum communication protocols.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
